key_insight: Mesh4D encodes an entire object's animation from a monocular video into a compact latent code so a feed‑forward model can reconstruct complete 3D shape and per-frame motion (as a deformation field) in one pass.
problem_solved: Reconstructing temporally consistent, complete 3D shape and motion of a dynamic object from a single-camera video — an ill-posed and computationally expensive task that typically requires multi-view inputs or slow optimization.
method: Feed-forward neural model that takes a monocular video and predicts a deformation field representing per-frame mesh motion and complete 3D geometry.
Compact latent space that encodes the whole animation sequence in a single code, learned with an autoencoder to enable one-pass inference.
Training guided by object skeletal structure to provide strong priors on plausible motion and deformations, improving robustness and realism.
impact: Enables fast, single-pass reconstruction and tracking of dynamic 3D meshes from everyday monocular videos, lowering the barrier for animation, AR/VR content creation, and real-time 3D tracking in ML pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: monocular video → encoder → compact latent code → decoder → per-frame mesh + deformation field
Before/after frames: input RGB frames side-by-side with reconstructed 3D mesh overlays (multiple time steps)

paper_title: Mesh4D: 4D Mesh Reconstruction and Tracking from Monocular Video
paper_authors: Zeren Jiang, Chuanxia Zheng, Iro Laina, Diane Larlus, Andrea Vedaldi
